_lane: LEVER 5 -- FLEET CONCENTRATION (are we five bets or one bet in five sizes?)

_population.filter: attribution=='engine' AND is_option AND NOT is_crypto
_population.n_small_note: 26 ET dates. Every cross-arm statistic here is n<=26 days. There is NO second population: the 391-day replay is ONE arm and structurally cannot express a fleet effect.
_population.scope_note: SPY OPTIONS ONLY -- excludes the crypto-twin residual, so per-arm and per-day totals differ by cents-to-dollars from the all-in figures in the briefing (e.g. Wed risky-3 -1458.00 here vs -1462.29 all-in). Both correct, different scopes.

q1_correlation._question: Five bets, or one bet in five sizes?
q1_correlation._dr_note: sd(sum of arms) / sum(sd of each arm). 1.0 = perfectly correlated, 0.408 = 6 independent equal-sd arms. TWO conventions given because they differ materially: 'traded_days_only' computes each arm's sd over the days IT traded (the honest per-arm volatility); 'zeros_filled' scores a non-trading day as 0.00 (LANE 0's convention, which understates a sporadic arm's sd and therefore INFLATES the ratio). Neither is wrong; quoting one without naming it is.

participation_vs_outcome._question: Do MORE arms on a day mean a WORSE day? (if not, a cap is aimed backwards)

size_vs_per_contract_edge_within_wave._question: Is the LARGEST position in a wave systematically the WORST per contract?
size_vs_per_contract_edge_within_wave._interpretation: negative r == the fleet systematically puts the most contracts behind the worst-performing exit configuration.

q2_book_tail._question: What does the correlation do to the BOOK-level daily loss tail?

decorrelated_fleet_bootstrap._method: each arm's own realized daily P&L permuted within its own traded days, independently per arm, re-summed by day. Marginals + participation preserved exactly; ONLY the cross-arm common factor is destroyed.

q2_book_tail._capital_matched_note: Each arm's OWN realized per-contract P&L for the day, multiplied by the FLEET's total contract count that day. Answers: if all the money ran through ONE arm's decisions, how fat is the tail? Real per-contract dollars, real contract counts, no model.

q3c_concurrency_cap._question: Only N of 5 arms may hold the same contract simultaneously (N=1,2,3).

concurrency_profile._question: Where in the concentration spectrum do the dollars actually sit?
concurrency_profile._headline: If this table slopes UP with concurrency, an arm-concurrency cap is aimed at the profitable end of the book and cannot be the loss-magnitude instrument.

q3c_concurrency_cap._priority_rule: FCFS by exact broker fill timestamp (microsecond). This is the only priority rule that is live-implementable without a new arbiter, but note it is a RACE: several clusters have two arms filling in the SAME second. The tie-break sweep below is therefore not decoration -- it is the honesty check on the whole cell.

cap_1.verdict: NO SELECTIVE SKILL -- indistinguishable from removing the same number of trades at random

cap_3.verdict: NO SELECTIVE SKILL -- indistinguishable from removing the same number of trades at random

q3c_ext_fleet_entry_cap._question: Cap TOTAL fleet entries per (date, contract), any arm.

q3b_exit_stagger._question: Do the arms' different TP1s / exit shapes actually buy anything?

_labels.best_uniform_ORACLE: ORACLE BOUND -- requires knowing ex-ante which arm's exit config wins. NOT live-executable.
_labels.dispersion_value_vs_mean: The live, realized value of having different exit configs across arms. Signed. This IS the answer to task 3(b).

random_config_assignment_null._method: shuffle WHICH arm's realized per-contract outcome lands on WHICH arm's realized quantity, within each wave. Tests whether the current config-to-size pairing is better than a coin flip.

q4_silent_arms._question: Is the fleet better or worse off for having bold-2 and safe-3 dark?

participation_audit.BRIEF_CORRECTION: The task brief states bold-2 and safe-3 have 'four consecutive zero-trade sessions'. Broker fills say TWO (2026-08-05 and 2026-08-06) for BOTH arms -- each has real engine option fills on 2026-08-04. Reported as measured. (The '4th session' framing in EOD-2026-08-06-SILENT-ARMS counts consecutive EOD lenses written, not zero-fill sessions.)

silence_netting._convention: POSITIVE = the silence HELPED the fleet (a loss avoided). NEGATIVE = the silence COST the fleet (a gain forgone).

cross_check_thursday_published.method: real OPRA 1-min bars through live exit_manager.plan_exit_actions (that lens's own harness), parity-checked against safe-2 broker truth at 2.4% error
cross_check_thursday_published.note: TWO INDEPENDENT METHODS on the same day. This lane substitutes a config-matched sibling's REALIZED per-contract result (pure ledger arithmetic, no exit model); the published lens replays real OPRA through the live exit core. They should agree in sign and rough magnitude, and the published figure is the better one -- quote THAT for Thursday.

counterfactual_full_week_if_both_arms_ha._label: n=2 dark sessions. NOT an evidence bar. Direction only.
